name: r6-contact-pair-live
description: THE CONTACT PAIR v2, arm 1 of 3 — `noDamage: FALSE`, and the arm that DIES. R5's pair proved the game does something the guard was hiding; it could not say WHAT, because the model carried no damage. R6 slice 3 carries it, so this arm's whole 130-tick stream is a claim about numbers. Booted at (32,128) so the spawn (40,136) is level with `sandtrap@96,128`'s ENTITY CENTRE (104,136), and RIGHT is held for every one of the 130 ticks — both choices load-bearing. Level with the centre, `center.y` is 0, so `Player.knockback`'s y branch (`Math.abs(center.y) > 0.5`) drops the impulse and the x branch (`>=`) keeps it: every knockback here is a PURE -3.00 px/tick shove west, which is what lets the held RIGHT walk straight back in. Held throughout, the 20-tick steering loss is DIRECTLY visible as the gap between hits (`Player.input`'s four arrow branches sit inside `if (hitsTimer <= 0)`), which R5's tape could not show — its last RIGHT was at tick 46 and its hit landed at 50, so no held key was left to lose. Three hits at 48 / 72 / 100, `hits >= hitsMax` on the third, and then the thing no tape on this ladder has ever crossed: `Player.die()` -> `Game.restartLevel()` -> `FP.world = new Game(8, 32, 128)`, a GAME-INITIATED world reboot the driver did not order, landing the player back at (40,136) with `hits` and `hitsTimer` fresh. The remaining 30 ticks are the respawn walking again, and they stop short of the fourth hit at 147 on purpose — one death, stated.
